text.headline: Consumer apps are adding logo walls
text.deck: Logo walls are getting more common on consumer app homepages, while their share across tracked homepages is roughly flat.
body: Headspace, Readwise and Canva are among the 8 of 29 tracked consumer app homepages that show a wall of logos. Across the full set, we found logo walls on 127 of 281 homepages.

Logo walls are still less common on consumer app homepages than in the full set, but the gap is narrowing. Their share among consumer apps is gaining 1.3 percentage points a quarter, against 0.4 points a quarter across all tracked homepages.

text.headline: Homepages put the scroll to work
text.deck: Scroll-driven animation appeared on 88 of 300 tracked homepages in the latest quarter. Its share was flat.
body: On Netlify, Allbirds and R/GA, scrolling does more than move the page: it drives the animation. Across the tracked homepages, the share using that technique came to 29.3% in the latest quarter.

That share held steady for the quarter. Over time, though, scroll-driven animation has gained ground at a pace of 1.3 percentage points a quarter. That puts it in the top tenth of the patterns we track for momentum.

text.headline: Dev tools are putting charts on their homepages
text.deck: Charts or data visuals appear on 9 of 30 tracked dev tools homepages. The sector’s share is gaining 1.2 percentage points a quarter.
body: Tailwind CSS, Astro and Cloudflare all show charts or data visuals on their homepages. Across the full set of 281 tracked homepages we looked at, just 17 show them, dev tools included.
The share of homepages with charts or data visuals is growing across the full set, too, but by 0.1 percentage points a quarter. In dev tools, the pace is picking up.

text.headline: Coinbase added agents to its headline
text.deck: Between 11 and 14 November, Coinbase replaced “Trusted by millions worldwide” with “The trusted financial account for you and your agents”. Its homepage also went from video to a still.
body: Trust stayed in the headline, but the crowd dropped out. The old line told you how many people trusted Coinbase. The new one names the product, a financial account, and says who it’s for: you and your agents.
The homepage also says “Trade stocks around the clock”. That line names something you can do with the account. The headline leaves open what the agents do.
text.how_we_know: The headline and hero changes were measured from captures on 11 and 14 November; the AI figures are our read of homepage copy, an AI estimate.

text.headline: Homepages are making room for agents
text.deck: Agent, agents or agentic appears in the headline on 16 of 162 tracked homepages whose headline we can read.
body: Between 11 and 14 November, Coinbase went from “Trusted by millions worldwide” to “The trusted financial account for you and your agents”. Trust stayed in the line. The agents are new.
Between 11 and 13 November, MongoDB replaced “ONE DATA PLATFORM. UNLIMITED AI POTENTIAL.” with “Every scale. Every agent. One platform”.
At Slack, agents are colleagues: “All your people and AI agents working together”. At Cursor, the agent is the product: “Cursor is your coding agent for building ambitious software.”
text.how_we_know: The count and copy changes were measured from homepage captures between 11 and 20 November.

text.headline: Sale copy turns up on buttons too
text.deck: On 20 November, sale copy appeared on 11 of 229 tracked homepages whose headline or buttons we can read.
body: Equinox leads with access rather than a price: “Black Friday Early Access”. Brooklinen puts the discount first in “25% Off Sitewide Black Friday Sale”. Parachute skips the occasion and goes straight to “20% Off Everything”.
On the buttons, Casper keeps it to “Shop sale” and GoPro goes with “Shop Deals”. Neither names a price. Olipop fits the discount into the button itself: “Shop 50% Off”.
